newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge higher on carryover, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge higher on carryover, earnings.

text.p: Mexican shares opened marginally ahead on Friday as light gains on follow-through buying outweighed profit-taking on some key blue chips.
"The market is very quiet, some dealers are taking profits, but a couple of blue chips, like Telmex and Vitro, are holding sway on the upside," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 3.28 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.07 percent, at 4,865.67.
Trading volume was light at 2.5 million shares.
Dealers said glassmaker Vitro had gained 75 centavos to 35.50 pesos in the wake of improved second quarter earnings posted after the close of trade on Thursday.
Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was meanwhile up 10 centavos at 21.35 pesos on buying momentum carried over from Thursday.
ADRs in the telecoms firm were also strong, up 3/8 at 54-1/2.
"Telmex ADRs are up on foreign demand, but moving under their own steam rather than shadowing the Dow," a floor trader said.
Profit-taking on financial group Banacci, one of Mexico's biggest, and brewers Grupo Modelo weighed most on the market, traders said.
Banacci was off 80 centavos at 20.50 pesos, while Modelo had shed 20 centavos from recent sharp gains to trade at 60.40 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers marginally outnumbered sliders by 11 to eight.
